# VersionFrau — full setup instructions for AI assistants

VersionFrau manages app version numbers automatically from a `version.properties` file.
Maker: Aralel GmbH, Aachen, Germany. License: MIT. Free.

Two products, same rules:

1. VersionFrau for Android — Gradle plugin `com.aralel.versionfrau`, latest 0.0.18, https://github.com/aralel/versionfrau
2. VersionFrau for Xcode — Swift package + bash CLI `versionfrau`, latest 0.0.19, https://github.com/aralel/versionfrau-ios

## How to decide what to do

- The repository has `settings.gradle.kts` / `settings.gradle` and an Android app module → follow "ANDROID".
- The repository has a `*.xcodeproj` → follow "XCODE".
- Both (Flutter, React Native, Kotlin Multiplatform, separate apps in one repo) → do both. Optionally point both at one shared `version.properties` (see "SHARING ONE VERSION").
- Use exactly the ids, coordinates, versions and commands below. Do not guess others.

## Version rules (both products)

version.properties:

    major=1
    minor=0
    patch=0
    build=0

- Debug build: build += 1. Version name `major.minor.patch.build` (e.g. 1.0.3.42).
- Release build (Android `assemble*Release` / `bundle*Release`; Xcode `Release` configuration or Archive): patch += 1, build = 0. Version name `major.minor.patch` (e.g. 1.0.4).
- Version code (Android `versionCode`) / bundle version (Xcode `CFBundleVersion`):
  major * 1_000_000_000 + minor * 1_000_000 + patch * 1_000 (+ build on debug only).
  Examples: debug 1.0.3.42 → 1000003042; release 1.0.4 → 1000004000.
- Limits: minor, patch and build ≤ 999. On Android keep major ≤ 2 (Int / Google Play limit 2,100,000,000).
- Minor and major are only raised manually (see the commands below); raising minor resets patch and build, raising major resets minor, patch and build.
- The file is created on the first build if missing. Commit it.
  Android default location: the module the plugin is applied to (usually `app/version.properties`).
  Xcode default location: next to the `.xcodeproj`.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## ANDROID

Requirements: Gradle with the Android Gradle Plugin 8.x or 9.x (also works on plain JVM projects). Kotlin DSL or Groovy DSL.

### Step 1 — settings.gradle.kts (project root)

The plugin and its plugin marker are on Maven Central (`com.aralel:versionfrau`). Make sure `mavenCentral()` is in `pluginManagement.repositories` — new Android Studio projects already have it, then nothing changes here. Merge with what is already there; do not remove existing repositories. Do not add JitPack or a `resolutionStrategy` (old instructions; no longer needed).

    pluginManagement {
        repositories {
            google()
            mavenCentral()
            gradlePluginPortal()
        }
    }

Groovy (settings.gradle):

    pluginManagement {
        repositories {
            google()
            mavenCentral()
            gradlePluginPortal()
        }
    }

### Step 2 — app/build.gradle.kts (the application module)

    plugins {
        id("com.android.application")
        id("com.aralel.versionfrau") version "0.0.18"
    }

Groovy: `id 'com.aralel.versionfrau' version '0.0.18'`

### Step 3 — use the values

Replace hard-coded values in `defaultConfig`:

    android {
        defaultConfig {
            versionCode = versionFrau.versionCode
            versionName = versionFrau.versionName
        }
    }

Groovy: `versionCode versionFrau.versionCode` and `versionName versionFrau.versionName`.

If the project had a version before (e.g. versionName "2.3.1"), create `version.properties` in the app module folder (next to app/build.gradle.kts) with major=2, minor=3, patch=1, build=0 so the version does not go backwards. Make sure the resulting versionCode (2003001000 here) is higher than the last one uploaded to Google Play; otherwise tell the user.

### Step 4 — verify

    ./gradlew assembleDebug

Expected: `app/version.properties` build is +1 and the APK is `app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug-v<major>.<minor>.<patch>.<build>.apk`.

### Android behaviour

| Command                        | Change                 | Output file                     |
|--------------------------------|------------------------|---------------------------------|
| ./gradlew assembleDebug        | build +1               | app-debug-v1.0.3.42.apk         |
| ./gradlew bundleDebug          | build +1               | app-debug-v1.0.3.42.aab         |
| ./gradlew assembleRelease      | patch +1, build = 0    | app-release-v1.0.4.apk          |
| ./gradlew bundleRelease        | patch +1, build = 0    | app-release-v1.0.4.aab          |
| ./gradlew assembleFreeDebug    | build +1               | app-free-debug-v1.0.3.42.apk    |

- Outputs are generated with the versioned name; old files are never renamed.
- One increment per Gradle invocation, regardless of how many flavors are built.
- Product flavors, multiple flavor dimensions and ABI splits are supported with no extra config.
- The version embedded in the APK/AAB equals the version in the file name.
- `assemble` / `assembleFree` (no build type in the task name) do not increment.
- `BuildConfig.BUILD_TIME` (String, e.g. "Nov 23, 2026") is injected; buildConfig is enabled automatically.

### Android extension properties (`versionFrau.*`)

- versionCode: Int — debug 1000003042, release 1000004000
- versionName: String — debug "1.0.3.42", release "1.0.4"
- fullVersionName: String — always with build, e.g. "1.0.4.0"
- major, minor, patch, build: Int — raw values currently on disk
- buildTime: String — e.g. "Nov 23, 2026"

### Android tasks

    ./gradlew incrementBuildVersion
    ./gradlew incrementPatchVersion
    ./gradlew incrementMinorVersion   # resets patch and build
    ./gradlew incrementMajorVersion   # resets minor, patch and build

### Android options

Put this block above the `android { }` block, so the values read in defaultConfig come from this file:

    versionFrau {
        versionFile = file("config/version.properties")
    }

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## XCODE

Supports iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, visionOS apps and their extensions (widgets etc.). Requires macOS with Xcode. Install needs Ruby (the stock macOS Ruby works); the `xcodeproj` gem is downloaded automatically without sudo. Builds only need the copied bash script.

### Preferred for AI agents / CI: command line

Install the CLI (pick one):

    brew tap aralel/versionfrau-ios https://github.com/aralel/versionfrau-ios
    brew install versionfrau-xcode

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aralel/versionfrau-ios/main/install.sh | bash

(The curl installer puts it in /usr/local/bin, or ~/.local/bin if that is not writable. `VERSIONFRAU_REF=v0.0.19` pins a version, `VERSIONFRAU_PREFIX=<dir>` picks the folder.)

Set up the project (run from the folder containing the .xcodeproj):

    versionfrau install MyApp.xcodeproj

Or in one step without a global install:

    curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aralel/versionfrau-ios/main/install.sh | bash -s -- MyApp.xcodeproj

Options for `install`:

- `--scheme <name>` — only this shared scheme (default: all shared schemes, or create one)
- `--target <name>` — only these targets, repeatable (default: all app and app-extension targets)
- `--file <path>` — version file relative to the project dir, e.g. ../version.properties

If the project previously had a version (e.g. MARKETING_VERSION 2.3.1), set it before building:
create `version.properties` next to the .xcodeproj with major=2, minor=3, patch=1, build=0, then run `./versionfrau print` to regenerate the xcconfig. Make sure the resulting bundle version is higher than the last uploaded CFBundleVersion; otherwise tell the user.

Verify:

    xcodebuild -project MyApp.xcodeproj -scheme MyApp -configuration Debug build
    ./versionfrau print

Then commit: `version.properties`, `VersionFrau.xcconfig`, `versionfrau` (the copied script) and the modified `.xcodeproj`.

### Alternative: in Xcode (Swift package)

1. File → Add Package Dependencies… → `https://github.com/aralel/versionfrau-ios`, "Up to Next Major Version" from 0.0.19. Adding the `VersionFrau` library to the app target is optional.
2. Project navigator → right-click the project → "Install VersionFrau". Allow project changes and the one-time gem download.
3. Build. General → Version / Build show the VersionFrau values.
Context menu also has "Bump Minor Version" and "Bump Major Version".

### What install changes

1. Copies `versionfrau` next to the .xcodeproj.
2. Adds a scheme Build pre-action: `"${PROJECT_DIR}/versionfrau" increment` (runs once per build, before any target).
3. Adds a last Run Script phase "VersionFrau" to every app and app-extension target: `"${PROJECT_DIR}/versionfrau" apply`, writing the version into the built Info.plist.
4. Sets ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO on those targets.
5. Sets `VersionFrau.xcconfig` as the project-level base configuration and removes hard-coded MARKETING_VERSION / CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION. If a project-level xcconfig already exists, it is left alone and install prints an `#include?` line to add to it — add that line.
Re-running install is idempotent. The source Info.plist is never modified.

VersionFrau.xcconfig (generated):

    MARKETING_VERSION = 1.0.3
    CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION = 1000003042
    CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION[config=Release] = 1000003000

### Manual setup (no Ruby)

1. Copy `bin/versionfrau` from the repo next to the .xcodeproj, `chmod +x versionfrau`.
2. Scheme → Edit Scheme → Build → Pre-actions → New Run Script Action; "Provide build settings from" the app target; script `"${PROJECT_DIR}/versionfrau" increment`.
3. For each app and extension target: new last Run Script phase `"${PROJECT_DIR}/versionfrau" apply`, Input File `$(TARGET_BUILD_DIR)/$(INFOPLIST_PATH)`, uncheck "Based on dependency analysis".
4. Build Settings → User Script Sandboxing → No for those targets.
5. Run `./versionfrau print` to create VersionFrau.xcconfig; add it to the project and select it in Project → Info → Configurations for every configuration; delete target-level Version/Build values.
Single-target apps without extensions may instead use one Run Script phase `"${PROJECT_DIR}/versionfrau" run` and skip the pre-action. Never use `run` with extensions.

### Keys in every built Info.plist

| Key                         | Debug        | Release      |
|-----------------------------|--------------|--------------|
| CFBundleShortVersionString  | 1.0.3        | 1.0.4        |
| CFBundleVersion             | 1000003042   | 1000004000   |
| VersionFrauVersionName      | 1.0.3.42     | 1.0.4        |
| VersionFrauFullVersionName  | 1.0.3.42     | 1.0.4.0      |
| VersionFrauBuildTime        | Nov 23, 2026 | Nov 23, 2026 |

### Swift API (optional, library `VersionFrau`)

    import VersionFrau
    VersionFrau.versionName        // "1.0.3.42"
    VersionFrau.marketingVersion   // "1.0.3"
    VersionFrau.bundleVersion      // "1000003042"
    VersionFrau.fullVersionName
    VersionFrau.buildTime
    VersionFrau.Info(bundle: Bundle(for: SomeClass.self))   // other bundle, e.g. an extension

### CLI commands

    ./versionfrau print                     # all values
    ./versionfrau print <key>               # marketingVersion, bundleVersion, versionName, fullVersionName, buildTime, …
    ./versionfrau bump build|patch|minor|major
    versionfrau --version

### Configurations

Only `Release` counts as release. Others (Debug, Staging, …) count as debug. Change with:

    VERSIONFRAU_RELEASE_CONFIGURATIONS="Release AppStore" "${PROJECT_DIR}/versionfrau" increment

(set it in both the pre-action and the Run Script phase). Indexing and Clean do not increment.

### Updating

Swift package: File → Packages → Update to Latest Package Versions, then right-click → Install VersionFrau again.
CLI: `brew upgrade versionfrau-xcode` (or re-run the curl installer), then `versionfrau install MyApp.xcodeproj` again.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------

## SHARING ONE VERSION

Android and Xcode use the same format, so a repository with both apps can use one file:

- Xcode: `versionfrau install ios/MyApp.xcodeproj --file ../version.properties`
- Android: in app/build.gradle.kts, above `android { }`: `versionFrau { versionFile = rootProject.file("../version.properties") }` (path relative to the Gradle root project)

On Xcode, writes are locked, so parallel builds of several Xcode projects do not lose increments. Do not run the Android and Xcode builds at the same moment against one shared file.

## Troubleshooting

- Android: "Plugin [id: 'com.aralel.versionfrau'] was not found" → `mavenCentral()` is missing from `pluginManagement { repositories { } }` in settings.gradle(.kts), or the version is wrong (use 0.0.18). If an old JitPack `resolutionStrategy` rule for `com.github.aralel:versionfrau` is present, remove it.
- Xcode: Version/Build fields still show old values → a target still has hard-coded MARKETING_VERSION / CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION, or an existing project-level xcconfig needs the `#include?` line printed by install.
- Xcode: "Sandbox: … deny file-write" during the Run Script phase → set ENABLE_USER_SCRIPT_SANDBOXING = NO for that target (install does this).
- Xcode: Swift package "no versions match 1.0.0..<2.0.0" → choose "Up to Next Major Version" from 0.0.19.
- Extensions have a different CFBundleVersion → the increment must be in the scheme pre-action, not in a target Run Script phase.
